name: Wood type
summary: Large display letters routed from end-grain wood instead of cast in metal, so posters and bills can use letters 5–50 cm high at a low cost.
how: Use wood type for letters above about 72 pt, where metal is too heavy and too expensive.
Draw the faces to be loud at a distance: fat face, slab and condensed grotesque, in one weight per line.
Mix several faces and sizes on one bill and centre each line, as the job printers did.

origin.note: Darius Wells makes wood type in quantity with a routing machine, and the poster printers take it up at once.

adoptions.via: The first wood type lines are fat faces copied from the London founders.
Wood type founders add Egyptian slabs and condensed letters for posters.
Trade cards and shop signs set the name of the firm in heavy wood letters.
